newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares closed at a new record high on Wednesday as underlying positive market sentiment overcame early jitters about a weaker rand which put a dampener on industrials.
The overall index added 13.5 points to close at 7,107.7, a new all time peak for the second day running, helped up largely by a buoyant gold board.

"The industrial market is looking slightly firmer after trading narrowly mixed. They did not make as much progress as they made yesterday and probably the single biggest factor was the currency," one dealer said.
The rand came off the day's weakest levels as the market continued to consolidate after a jittery start on Wednesday following the currency's eight-cent slide on Tuesday.
It was last at 4.4740/4790 against the dollar from 4.4490/4540 overnight.
"Whenever the rand weakens, the feel is it will prompt overseas investors to do a lot of (stock) selling. Yesterday (Wednesday) buying was aggressive but that has been absent today," one dealer said.
"The underlying sentiment is positive and that held up the market," another one said.
The industrial index crept up 1.1 points to close at 8,369.2 while golds jumped 32.8 points to 1,481.6. About 720 million shares exchanged hands on Wednesday, up from Tuesday's 661 million.
"Golds were very much the flavour of the day because of the weaker rand," one dealer said.
"The gold price just about held up its own around the $346.25(/ounce) level today and that also helped the golds," another one said.
The dealers said currency movements on Thursday and the bullion price would determine trade on gold counters while industrials were expected to settle down a bit, taking their cue from Wall Street.
Anglos dipped 1.50 rand to 275 rand, de Beers gained 50 cents to 150.50 rand and Val Reefs leapt nine rand to 340 rand.
On the futures market, the all-share March contract was at 6,500/10 from 6,523, industrials contract was at 8,143/50 from 8,152 while golds contract was at 1,032/45 from 1,018.
